overview: Black answers 1.Nf3 with ...d6, aiming for a Pirc, Philidor or Old Indian set-up with ...Nf6, ...g6 or ...e5. White usually takes the centre with d4 and e4 or plays c4 and g3. It mostly transposes to Pirc, Philidor or Indian structures and is a flexible, non-committal way to reply.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 and e4 to take the centre and transpose to a Pirc/Philidor with an extra Nf3
Or c4 and g3 for a Reti/English set-up

black_ideas.idea: Flexible development with ...Nf6, ...g6, ...Bg7 or ...e5 depending on White's set-up
Delay committing the centre pawns and hit White's centre later with ...e5 or ...c5

typical_structures.structure: Pirc/Philidor or King's Indian-type structures after White builds a centre; Hypermodern

character.notes: Not clearly forcing or particularly solid; it depends on the set-up chosen. I am unsure what the dominant continuation is.

soundness.notes: Sound; just a slow, passive-looking reply.

structure.notes: Not decided; transposes into many structures.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players against 1.Nf3.

level.notes: Black has to choose plans from several set-ups; little to memorise.

character.reason: Flexible and transposing, not forcing and not especially rigid.

structure.reason: Nothing is fixed after two moves; flank-style flexibility.

level.reason: Needs plans from several structures but little theory.

plans.reason: Black leaves the centre to White and attacks it later with a fianchetto.
